To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) killer activity and immunity are associated with two segments of the dsRNA genome, (ii) the killer protein of the P4 virus is required to exclude the genome of the P6 killer, (iii) the information for viral coat formation is associated with the heaviest components of the dsRNAs, and (iv) the information for the killer protein and for the immunity to P6 are located in two different segments of the genome.
the killer phenomenon in the smut fungus Ustilago is caused by a virus and that the killer protein is involved in the exclusion of the genomes of other killer viruses.

the killer protein of U. maydis P4 is a product of a segment that maps to the lightest segment in the genome of the virus and that it is associated with the ability of the virus to exclude the genome of the P6 virus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the genetic information of the dsRNA viruses associated with the P1-P6 killer systems of U. maydis.
the mapping of functions in dsRNA viruses.
the mapping of viral functions and the analysis of the genetic control of the expression of the P4 and P6 viruses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the killer phenomenon in U. maydis involves at least 2 viral functions, a killer protein and a killer RNA segment, that are associated with different segments of the dsRNA genome.

the dsRNA genomes of the killer viruses of Ustilago contain information for the synthesis of a killer toxin and a killer immunity protein and that they are organized in such a way that they can also exclude the genomes of other killer viruses.
the P6 killer function resides in a segment in the heavy group of the dsRNA genome and is not related to the killer function of P4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the P6 killer system is a “virus” and that the killer function of the P4 system is associated with a “viral” component.

the P4 killer phenomenon is associated with the presence of a specific segment of dsRNA in the virus associated with this killer specifity and that the killer protein of the P4 virus is involved in the exclusion mechanism.
the killer phenomenon is associated with the presence of a specific dsRNA molecule in the cytoplasm of the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dsRNA genome can be organized in such a way that the information for coat formation and killer activity can be separated from the information that is required for the exclusion of specific viral genomes.
we have identified a new phenomenon in Ustlilago, the killer phenomenon.
the killer phenomenon in the smut fungus Ustilago is not a simple case of “gene transfer”.
